rows.reason: Fault fixed: line 10 is now said only to compare the tunnel to a 'carriage-drive' other animals own; 'pop!' (l.14) and 'in the warm grass of a great meadow' (l.15) verbatim on the cited lines; hedge (l.21) and river (l.29) do come later.
Fault fixed: 'danced every dance' (l.37) is now attributed to Mr Bingley; Mr Darcy at end of l.39, 'once' / 'once with Miss Bingley' verbatim on l.40; one with each makes two, matching the key.

Fault fixed: 'a good six miles' is now tied to reaching the wooden bridge again (l.30-31), not added to the way home; 'can't drive over that tree, nor yet get round it' (l.29) and 'go back to the four crossways' (l.30) verbatim and set aside the round-the-tree option. Question judged sound: the key's 'six miles further' is a loose paraphrase of 'a good six miles before we get round to the wooden bridge again', but it is the only option lines 29-31 support (no driving round, no waiting, no walking home), so no question fault.

Fault fixed: 'hopes his leg's better' is a hope, correctly cited across lines 13 and 14, and the leg is shown to be Mr Goggles's, not Pa's, which sets aside the attribute-transfer option; the one question 'will he lend him his spirit-level' is verbatim on l.14.

Fault fixed: no invented feeling, and 'that one on Monday' and 'get out of spellings' are kept together as what Miss said (l.41); 'You've missed a cupboard' (l.40) and 'In the annexe' (across 40-41, cited as such) verbatim; Friday option set aside.

Fault fixed: no claim of standing; 'no water in their room' (l.8), 'under the spout of the pump' (across 9-10, cited as such), 'One pumped and the other washed' and 'splashy but interesting' (l.10) verbatim; key drawn from the line, splashing option set aside. Question judged sound: the stem's 'the girls' is an inference the passage supports (Roberta wakes Phyllis, Peter is in another room, 'their room', 'One pumped and the other washed' = two people), and the key is the only defensible option, so no question fault.

Fault fixed: no 'borrow'; the things are their own, used because they 'could not find all the right things' (l.21); 'a glass ash-tray made an excellent salt-cellar' (across 21-22, cited as such) and 'a newish baking-tin' / 'to put bread on' (l.22) verbatim; fire and kettle (l.20) set aside.

Fault fixed: 'Below' and 'further along' are now quoted; 'a boat lay in the mud with its ribs showing' (l.20), 'a gull standing on it' and 'further along' (l.21) verbatim; posts correctly placed further along.
